subject: Market reset: offer structure and integration feasibility
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@datacove.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Competitive ask + RFP comparison attached

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile on streaming looked solid. We're in parallel conversations with FluxAI and they sent us a commercial that's materially lower on list price for our run volume.

Attached is a short spreadsheet (RFP_Comparison.xlsx) that our procurement team built comparing FluxAI's line-item to the numbers you quoted during the proof-of-concept. Two asks from our side:

- Can Redwood clearly map to the same billable units and provide a like-for-like price match (or an alternative packaging) for our expected 24M tokens/month?
- We also need a quick integration feasibility note: can we replicate current inference endpoints with no code changes (we're running a grpc-based client and heavy use of KV-cache features)?

If you can get back to us with a short pricing runbook and an SKU-level comparison, procurement would like to decide within the week. I'm cc'ing purchasing@procurement.datacove.ai for timelines.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
VP, Product
DataCove

—
Attachment: RFP_Comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Tara Singh <tara@datacove.ai>
Cc: purchasing@procurement.datacove.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T12:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Competitive ask + RFP comparison attached

Tara — thanks for the note and the sheet. Appreciate the clarity. Quick summary from our side and what I'll deliver:

1) Like-for-like mapping: we'll translate tokens -> request/response units the way your spreadsheet shows and produce a simple SKU-level comparison (tokens, embedding calls, and streaming sessions).
2) Price match options: two levers we can use — a 6-month pilot credit + committed run-rate discount, or an immediate list-price match on committed 12-month consumption. I'll outline both and the build/ops caveats.
3) Integration feasibility: initial read is positive — our runtime supports gRPC and KV cache semantics widely used. We'll confirm exact compatibility for your client version and any minor header translation required.

I'm looping in Jonas Weber (pricing lead) and Connor O'Brien (solutions eng) to validate the SKU mapping and SLO constraints. Kimberly Park from legal will take a quick look at procurement asks if we need a short sideletter.

I'll aim to send a concise one-page comparison + recommended path by EOD tomorrow. If procurement needs something faster (e.g., a redlineable sideletter), flag it and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

—
Attachment: redwood-market-reset-outline.pdf (one-page outline, 18KB)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T12:18:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Competitive ask + RFP comparison attached

Folks — forwarding DataCove's sheet and timeline. TL;DR: 24M tokens/month, gRPC client, expects like-for-like cost comparison vs FluxAI. Procurement wants decision within a week.

Outcomes we should propose (priority order):
- Option A: 90-day pilot w/ 50% pilot credit up to 10M tokens, then commit-to-buy at a 10% below FluxAI list (requires 12mo consumption commit).
- Option B: Immediate committed discount without pilot: 8% below FluxAI for 12mo, plus one-time migration credit to cover integration effort.
- Option C: If we can't match list, offer a packaging restructure (seat + token pool) that reduces overage risk and preserves KV cache SLA.

Tech asks for Connor: confirm whether our gRPC handshakes require client changes for the customer's KV cache usage pattern (they mention heavy prefix caching). Provide an ops estimate (days to migrate, risk factors).
Pricing asks for Jonas: translate their sheet rows to our SKUs and produce a like-for-like cost table, and tell me minimal discount to be price-competitive while preserving margin thresholds.
Legal: Kimberly — if procurement requests a short sideletter to lock price protections for the pilot, what's your minimum redlineable language and lead time?

Please reply with your bullets; I'll pull them into a one-pager and send to Tara + purchasing.

Rachel

Date: 2027-05-03T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Market reset: offer structure and integration feasibility

Rachel / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from procurement:

- We prefer a 90-day pilot (short term) but need an SLO for median inference latency <= 220ms and a written assurance that KV-cache behavior (prefix reuse) won't cause incorrect tokenization or stateful regressions.
- If Redwood can mirror FluxAI's effective per-token price for committed volumes, procurement will move to signature within 10 business days.
- Please include an initial SOW line-item for the migration effort (estimate hours + cost) so we can include it in the procurement packet.

Happy to review the one-pager when ready. If it's helpful, our procurement lead (purchasing@procurement.datacove.ai) is available for a 30-min slot tomorrow morning to go over final commercial terms.

Best,
Tara
VP, Product | DataCove
